title: Aircraft Forces in One Direction
learningObjectives: Calculate acceleration from net force and mass using F = m * a
Predict whether an aircraft rises, falls, accelerates, or slows when opposing forces are unbalanced

sources.title: Simplified Aircraft Motion — NASA Glenn Research Center, Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics

evidence.quote: Where a is the acceleration, m is the mass of the aircraft, and F is the net force acting on the aircraft.

explanations.text: Unbalanced forces cause acceleration, found by dividing net force by mass.

evidence.quote: The net force is the difference between the opposing forces; lift minus weight, or thrust minus drag.
If the forces become unbalanced, the aircraft will move in the direction of the greater force.

explanations.text: Net force is the difference between opposing forces, and motion follows the greater force.
More thrust than drag causes acceleration, while more drag than thrust causes slowing down.

predictions.prompt: A model aircraft with mass 5 kg has 10 N net force in the flight direction. Predict its acceleration.
A model aircraft with mass 2 kg has -10 N net force in the flight direction. Predict its acceleration.
